coverage: Approved date patterns, calendar month/year names and invariant fixed-offset notation from rounds 24–25. Specification data, not an implemented parser or fixed physical-unit catalog.

calendar.dateInputFormat.meaning: The universally accepted four-digit-year, two-digit-month, two-digit-day input pattern.
calendar.dateInputFormat.context: Round 24 accepts this Latin-baseline numeric date form in all interface languages. The active locale may add its explicitly approved pattern: Russian adds DD.MM.YYYY. Y, M and D are invariant pattern metacharacters, not literal input letters or words to translate. Future patterns require notation validation; adding a translation must not silently enable unrelated ambiguous date forms. Output is always YYYY-MM-DD, independently of the local input pattern.
calendar.dateInputFormat.location: Date-token recognition for the baseline and active locale, illustrated in calendar input help. The pattern itself is specification metadata rather than a new permanent interface label.

calendar.offsetInputFormat.meaning: A signed fixed-offset suffix for a clock time or date-time.
calendar.offsetInputFormat.context: Round 25. This pattern is invariant, not translated prose. ± means a literal + or - sign; HH and mm mean exactly two decimal digits, hours 00–23 and minutes 00–59. UTC stays uppercase. An input suffix may follow the time directly or after a space. The entire suffix/target is one construct, so its sign is not an arithmetic operator. Examples: +03:00, UTC-05:30. No regional-zone rules or general RFC compatibility is implied.
calendar.offsetInputFormat.location: Pattern metadata for calendar recognition, conversion-target completion and calendar help; pattern metacharacters are not literal text to paste.

calendar.offsetTargetFormat.meaning: A signed fixed-offset conversion target following :: or to.
calendar.offsetTargetFormat.context: Round 25. This pattern is invariant, not translated prose. ± means a literal + or - sign; HH and mm mean exactly two decimal digits, hours 00–23 and minutes 00–59. UTC stays uppercase. An input suffix may follow the time directly or after a space. The entire suffix/target is one construct, so its sign is not an arithmetic operator. Examples: +03:00, UTC-05:30. No regional-zone rules or general RFC compatibility is implied.
calendar.offsetTargetFormat.location: Pattern metadata for calendar recognition, conversion-target completion and calendar help; pattern metacharacters are not literal text to paste.

calendar.unit.month.meaning: A calendar month, whose day length depends on a starting date.
calendar.unit.month.context: Round 31 replaces the former Latin month spelling with mon, not an additional alias. The Latin baseline is always active; only the active interface locale adds its spelling, such as Russian мес. Protected calendar-unit name; no fixed seconds factor. m/м remain metre/minute and г remains gram. No additional declensions or aliases. The stable semantic identity calendar.unit.month is unchanged.
calendar.unit.month.location: Calendar-period unit positions in formulas, conversion targets, inline completion and result formatting. Names use the common completion alignment and description style.

calendar.unit.year.meaning: A calendar year represented by twelve calendar months.
calendar.unit.year.context: Round 25. Latin baseline always active, with only the active interface locale adding a spelling. Protected unit names. These are calendar units, not fixed seconds factors. m/м remain metre/minute and г remains gram. No additional declensions or aliases. Store stable semantic identities when changing locale.
calendar.unit.year.location: Calendar-period unit positions in formulas, conversion targets, inline completion and result formatting. Names use the common completion alignment and description style.

calendar.offset.utcSuffix.meaning: The zero fixed-offset suffix on a time or date-time.
calendar.offset.utcSuffix.context: Round 25. Invariant uppercase spelling in every locale; do not translate or add lowercase aliases. The suffix is used on clock/date-time literals and displayed explicit zero offsets. The target follows :: or to. Positive and negative numeric zero offsets both display Z. Date alone has no offset.
calendar.offset.utcSuffix.location: Calendar literal suffixes or conversion targets and related help/completion; not a new constant or permanent widget label.

calendar.offset.utcTarget.context: Round 25. Invariant uppercase spelling in every locale; do not translate or add lowercase aliases. The suffix is used on clock/date-time literals and displayed explicit zero offsets. The target follows :: or to. Positive and negative numeric zero offsets both display Z. Date alone has no offset.
calendar.offset.utcTarget.location: Calendar literal suffixes or conversion targets and related help/completion; not a new constant or permanent widget label.
